name: agent-skills

skills.example: before committing → a message that says what changed and why, in the voice of someone who was there.

skills.name: bible-study
skills.description: Use when the user says 'bible study', asks to study a passage, or wants a scholarly multi-translation study written into the vault under Areas/Bible Study.

skills.example: "study Romans 8" → multiple translations, the scholarly reading, and the disagreements named rather than smoothed over.

skills.example: photograph the bulletin → a sermon-notes file with the readings, liturgical date, and scaffolding to write into.

skills.name: codex-first

skills.example: a fully-specified refactor → handed to Codex with the spec, and the result verified before you see it.

skills.name: credit-routing
skills.description: Use at the start of any non-trivial task, when deciding whether to delegate, when a task has failed twice, before escalating model or effort, or when the user mentions credits, cost, tokens, routing, or 'which model'.
skills.summary: Decide what to delegate, to which model, at what effort — before starting the work.
skills.example: at the start of anything non-trivial → which model, what effort, and what to delegate, decided before the work starts.

skills.name: decision-sync

skills.example: after a decision is made → the reasoning filed into your vault with frontmatter, backlinks, and an index row.

skills.name: devrel-engine
skills.description: Use when the user asks for a DevRel program or strategy, a developer community plan, an ambassador or champion program, a talk or office-hours pipeline, or wants transcripts and community signals turned into prioritized DevRel actions. Camp
skills.summary: Turn transcripts and community signals into a prioritized DevRel program.
skills.example: paste a month of community signal → a prioritized program, not a summary.

skills.name: email-draft-review
skills.description: Use when the user says 'draft my email replies', 'handle my inbox', 'triage Gmail', or asks to prepare (never send) replies to the emails that need answers.
skills.summary: Triage an inbox and prepare replies — drafts only, never sends.
skills.example: "triage my inbox" → replies prepared for the mail that needs answers. Drafts only; it never sends.

skills.name: field-notes-draft
skills.description: Use when the user says 'Field Notes', asks for the Thursday or Friday Field Notes review, wants newsletter candidates ranked, or wants the Saturday issue drafted after picking a theme. Never sends or schedules.
skills.summary: Rank newsletter candidates from recent reading, then draft the issue once you pick a theme.
skills.example: "Field Notes" → three ranked themes from the week's reading; pick one and it drafts the issue.

skills.name: gatherer
skills.description: Use when the user says 'gather my work', 'what's on my plate', or 'daily gather', or when a review needs your open GitHub issues and PRs, watched Trac tickets, and Things tasks pulled into today's daily note.
skills.summary: Pull open issues, PRs, watched tickets, and tasks into today’s daily note.
skills.example: "what's on my plate?" → open issues, PRs, watched tickets and tasks pulled into today's note.

skills.name: github-profile
skills.description: Use when the user asks to improve, review, or set up a GitHub profile README, bio, pinned repos, or stats, or says 'make my GitHub profile look good'. Personal or organization profiles.
skills.summary: Improve a GitHub profile README, bio, pinned repos, and stats.
skills.example: "make my profile look good" → README, bio, pinned repos and stats that say what you actually do.

skills.name: github-repo

skills.example: "prepare this for open source" → the files a stranger needs before they will trust your repo.

skills.description: Use when the user says 'LMK when you're done', 'let me know', 'notify me', 'ping me when you're done', or says you is stepping away and wants a phone push when the work finishes.

skills.example: "LMK when you're done" → a phone push when the long job finishes, not a progress feed.

skills.summary: Scaffold a scheduled job so it inherits the maker/checker pattern from the start.
skills.example: "add an automation" → a scheduled job that inherits the maker/checker pattern instead of running unchecked.

skills.description: Use when asked to create or normalize shareable obsid.net links for Obsidian notes, convert obsidian:// links, or check the URL encoding of vault and file parameters.
skills.summary: Build and normalize shareable Obsidian links, with correct URL encoding.
skills.example: paste an obsidian:// link → a shareable URL with the vault and file parameters encoded correctly.

source_policy: Every entry points at the ORIGINAL source, never an intermediary. Where a skill reached this machine through a fork or a collection, the manifest names the upstream that actually published it and the fork is recorded separately. Two checks make that reliable: read the upstream's own credits before treating it as the origin, and never conclude 'no license' from the repo root alone — cursor/plugins has no root LICENSE but licenses each plugin directory, so the root check reports unlicensed for 44 skills that are in fact MIT.
usage_note: Run counts from the author's own transcripts over the window shown — how often each skill actually fired, not how useful it might be. A zero means it did not run in that window, which for recently-added skills means nothing yet.
